solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's simple, just put one's hand out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of put one's hand are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a task is easy: all you need do is reach out your hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' is a link; 'out' rearranges PUTONESHAND, where the possessive's S counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a case whose outcome is obvious, needing no debate, so straightforward.

clue.text: Member of the Police Force, if qualified

indicators.note: qualified means modified or altered, so the letters of force and if are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recruit joins the Police Force once properly qualified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like part of the definition, but the definition stops at 'Police'; 'qualified' rearranges FORCEIF.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman or policewoman is formally called a police constable or this.

clue.text: Relay arranged, in good time

indicators.note: the letters of relay are set out in a new order, as things are arranged

explanation.surface: A relay race has been organised to finish punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles RELAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: arriving before the due time means being ahead of schedule.

clue.text: Philosopher is alert to changes

indicators.note: the letters of is alert to undergo changes, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker remains watchful for any shift around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges ISALERTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek thinker who taught Alexander the Great, an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: Piece of boarded adornment

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a part taken from the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: A decorative wooden panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of' signals letters within 'boarded adornment'; read as a whole the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower part of an interior wall finished differently, often in wooden panelling.

clue.text: The better runners suffer a setback at the start of this race

definitions.text: The better runners suffer a setback at the start of this race

parts.words: The better runners suffer a setback at the start of this race
parts.note: in a race where stronger horses carry extra weight or start further back, the best entrants are deliberately held back

explanation.surface: The fastest athletes stumble right at the start of an event.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'setback' is not a mishap but a deliberate weight or distance imposed to even up the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in which the better competitors are given a disadvantage to equalise chances.

clue.text: Extract loan with skill

definitions.meaning: to ask someone for money, as in 'tap him for a fiver'
a deft manner of handling something, a light hand

explanation.surface: A borrower squeezes money out of a lender cleverly.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially one asks a friend for a loan this way; it also means a deft knack.

clue.text: Manage to define the bishop's position

definitions.meaning: a bishop presides above his diocese, so his place is placed 'above the diocese'

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to settle precisely where the bishop stands.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's diocese is his see, and he is set over it; split the answer into two words to read it so.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to supervise or direct work is to manage it.

clue.text: After a drink, game for battle!

indicators.note: after places the game piece following the drink piece in the answer

parts.note: water is a drink
loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: Following a beverage, someone is ready for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is an old gambling card game, not the British word for a lavatory here.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1815 battle in Belgium where Napoleon was finally defeated, an example of a battle.

clue.text: Bond fired at random, contrary to orders

indicators.note: the letters of bond fired are arranged in no set order, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Agent Bond shot wildly, ignoring his instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at random' rearranges BONDFIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited is against what orders permit.

clue.text: Practice for university man of learning

parts.note: a sage is a wise, learned man

explanation.surface: Rehearsal time for a university scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: custom or habitual practice is usage.

clue.text: Beast retiring with a broken toe

parts.note: coy means shy, retiring

indicators.note: the toe is broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal limps away shyly with an injured foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges TOE into OTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American wild dog, an example of a beast.

clue.text: Elevation above the peerage?

definitions.meaning: the royal style of address, for princes who rank above dukes and earls

explanation.surface: Someone asks about promotion to a rank higher than a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Means height or loftiness, and is also the royal form of address ranking above any peer.

clue.text: Call again to say one's piece

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to cite is to call, as summoning a witness

explanation.surface: Someone is summoned a second time to deliver a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The prefix meaning 'again' goes in front of the verb, as in re-cite, though the clue names it second.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to deliver a memorised poem or passage aloud before listeners.

clue.text: Royal Marine to order duck

parts.note: to command is to order
a duck is a zero score in cricket, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A marine is told to take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' means duck down as an order, but here is a nil score in cricket, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Marines are trained as these elite assault troops, so one marine is an example.

clue.text: French fortress, HQ until captured

indicators.note: the base piece captures the other, holding it inside

parts.note: headquarters is a base
till means until

explanation.surface: A French stronghold served as headquarters until it fell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' puts the until word inside the HQ word; 'HQ' is not a fortress clue here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789, an example of a French fortress.

clue.text: Evaluate performance of stroke on the river

indicators.note: on means the stroke piece is placed after the river piece

parts.note: the Test is a famous trout river in Hampshire, England
a drive is a stroke in golf or cricket

explanation.surface: Testing a rowing stroke on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To trial a vehicle by driving it, so in general to assess how something performs.

clue.text: Being solvent, her career is taking off

definitions.meaning: a chemical solvent used to remove paint or varnish
a performer whose job is removing her clothes

explanation.surface: A woman in good financial health finds her career soaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a paint-removing solvent and an erotic dancer who undresses for an audience.

clue.text: Detains about a thousand supporters

indicators.note: the detaining word sits about the thousand, surrounding it

parts.note: to arrest is to detain
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Police hold a thousand fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M inside ARRESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rests for one's arms on a chair, things that support.

clue.text: Where lots go despite rising prices

definitions.text: Where lots go despite rising prices

parts.words: Where lots go despite rising prices
parts.note: items for sale are called lots, and bidding sends their prices up

explanation.surface: Plenty of shoppers still turn up though costs keep climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A public sale where items are sold to the highest bidder as bids rise.

clue.text: Like to run, being so inclined

parts.note: as means like
to lope is to run with a long stride

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys jogging when in the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Means on a slant, so literally tilted or inclined.

clue.text: Novel representation of one real English queen

indicators.note: a new or novel form of the letters of one real, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novel portrays a genuine English queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel representation of' rearranges ONEREAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Aquitaine and Eleanor of Castile were both queens of England.

clue.text: Comic actor holding a clerical appointment

indicators.note: the actor's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin was a famous silent comic actor

explanation.surface: A comedian takes up a church post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A inside CHAPLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman appointed to a regiment, college or hospital, a clerical appointee.

clue.text: Lowest number in Meadow Street

parts.note: a lea is a meadow in poetic usage

explanation.surface: The smallest house number is found in Meadow Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the smallest amount or lowest quantity.

clue.text: Stay around with the French in order to eat

indicators.note: around turns the stay word back to front

parts.note: to bide is to stay
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone lingers with French friends so as to dine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the stay word back to front; the definition reads as a purpose clause, 'fit for eating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Means fit to be eaten, in a state good enough for eating.

clue.text: Plant seen in Britain? That's right!

parts.note: Br is an abbreviation for Britain or British
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a plant grows in Britain and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny shrub such as wild rose, an example of a plant.

clue.text: State without a health centre

indicators.note: the answer sits in the centre of the words without a health, spanning them

explanation.surface: A US state that lacks a clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' signals letters lying in the middle of 'without a health'.
explanation.definitionFit: A western state of the USA, an example of a state.

clue.text: Home help needed in retreat in the country

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the help word is in retreat, going backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Domestic staff are needed at a country retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' reverses AID to DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Asian nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Aristocratic Irishman cut by Scot

indicators.note: the name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Patrick is a typical Irish man's name
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A noble Irishman is wounded by a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims PATRICK to PATRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a patrician is of noble birth, from the Roman aristocratic class.

clue.text: An Olympic runner before the official opening

definitions.text: An Olympic runner before the official opening

parts.words: An Olympic runner before the official opening
parts.note: the athlete who carries the flame through the stadium ahead of the Games being declared open

explanation.surface: An athlete competes before the Games have started.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who carries the Olympic flame, which arrives just before the Games open.
